title: Headache in flight (including high CO2)

differential.label: Tension-type headache
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis. The most common headache type reported on the ISS.

differential.label: Space adaptation headache
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis. Common in the first days of flight.

differential.label: Headache from high cabin CO2
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis. Check the CO2 reading and ask crewmates.

differential.label: Migraine-like headache
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis. More common in the first week.

differential.label: Stroke, bleeding in the brain or infection. Cannot be ruled out onboard. Needs flight surgeon review
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis.

tests.title: Danger sign check
tests.instruction: Ask if the headache started suddenly and was explosive. Check for slurred speech, vision change, weak arms or legs, loss of balance or confusion. Note yes or no.

tests.title: Pain score
tests.instruction: Stay restrained. Enter a pain score from 0 to 10.

tests.title: Body temperature
tests.instruction: Take a temperature with the oral thermometer and enter it.

tests.title: Systolic blood pressure
tests.instruction: Stay restrained. Read systolic blood pressure on the monitor and enter it.

tests.title: Diastolic blood pressure
tests.instruction: Stay restrained. Read diastolic blood pressure on the monitor and enter it.

tests.title: Heart rate
tests.instruction: Read heart rate on the monitor and enter it.

tests.title: Cabin CO2
tests.instruction: Read the cabin CO2 value on the vehicle display or ask the ground. Write down the number and the unit. Ask crewmates if they have headaches too.

immediateSteps.title: Check for danger signs first
immediateSteps.instruction: Do the danger sign check. If any answer is yes, call the flight surgeon now.

immediateSteps.title: Check the cabin CO2
immediateSteps.instruction: Read the CO2 value. Ask crewmates if they also have headaches.

immediateSteps.title: Move to an area with good airflow
immediateSteps.instruction: Move away from closed corners and sleep spots. Stay near moving air.

immediateSteps.title: Measure and enter readings
immediateSteps.instruction: Do the tests on this card. Enter each result.

immediateSteps.title: Send the case to the flight surgeon
immediateSteps.instruction: Continue to handoff and send the case. Include the CO2 value.

cautions: This card is not a diagnosis. It gives no doses. If any danger sign is present, do not take anything from the kit before you reach the flight surgeon. A fixed cabin sensor can miss a local pocket of CO2 near the face. Use any kit item only as the flight surgeon directs.
sourceNote: Researcher card, Pulseframe Batch 1, 2026-11-15. Built from NASA OCHMO-TB-004 (Carbon Dioxide), OCHMO-MTB-004 (Space Adaptation Sickness), NASA IMM data, van Oosterhout et al. 2024 (Neurology) and MedlinePlus. Not a NASA procedure. The airflow step is a team inference from the CO2 sources, not a NASA instruction. Pending second-person safety review.
redFlagsLifeThreat: Headache started suddenly and was explosive.
Slurred speech, vision change, weak arm or leg, loss of balance, confusion or memory loss.
redFlagsCallGround: Severe pain in one eye with redness in that eye.
New vision change with the headache.
More than one crew member has a headache, or the CO2 value is above the 3 mmHg one-hour limit.
Fever or stiff neck with the headache.

timeLimits.item: Headache getting worse over 24 hours: call the flight surgeon.
NASA-STD-3001 limits the 1-hour average cabin CO2 to no more than 3 mmHg. This is a design limit, not a personal symptom threshold.

whenGroundUnavailable.status: PARTIAL (historical rule found, no current rule)
whenGroundUnavailable.detail: The 2001 ISS medical checklist says that in an emergency or during loss of signal the crew begins treatment, then calls the surgeon as soon as possible. This is a 2001 rule. No current public NASA or ESA rule was found. No public NASA procedure covers headache care without ground contact. Looked in: OCHMO-TB-004, OCHMO-MTB-004, HRP 2017 evidence report, van Oosterhout 2024.
firstAidThatNeedsNoGround: Do the danger sign check and record it with the time.
Check CO2 and move to good airflow.
Repeat the danger sign check if the headache gets worse.
Send the case as soon as the link returns.

proposedKeys.reason: TB-004 ties headache to CO2 partial pressure in mmHg; no key exists
Danger sign check has no key

candidateItemNotes: All three ids are listed under Pain Reliever in inventory.json. MTB-004 names acetaminophen, aspirin and NSAIDs for SAS headache. Ibuprofen is an NSAID. No doses are given here.
